{
  "question_intent": "Understanding bank investment strategy and USCB income expectations",
  "main_topics": ["bank investment strategy", "USCB income expectations", "RoTE", "EPS growth", "distributions", "sustainability", "2028 financial outlook"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": true,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "So one, just coming back on the additional SCAs, I was actually a bit surprised by the 100% return on investment. So, I just really wanted to understand a bit better, like if the returns on that type of investment are so high, wouldn't the Group be doing that kind of investment in any case? And, why limit it at the amounts being done? And then secondly, in terms of USCB, just trying to understand also the split or the expectation then for the NII versus non-NII as we look forward. Because if I understood from the call, NII is in broadly the right place now. I think previously you mentioned at Q1 that you'd expect non-NII to build to about 20% of total income. And I think consensus is now actually at 24%? So I'm just wondering whether you also think the non-NII expectation going out to 2028 is also a little bit too high at the moment.",
  "answer_quote": "Okay. Thank you, Amit. Why don't I take those questions? So on the first one, this is a plan of balance. We're trying to get a balance between progressive returns, progressive distributions and investments in the business. And, you can see that balance in the first half. You can see that RoTE is 14.8%. You can see the EPS growth. You can see the growth in the distributions that I called out before. So we're really trying to ensure that, if you like, everybody shares in the momentum of the bank. And that's really important. And it would be just as easy for us to not make those investments at all, but we don't think that is the right thing for the long-term returns and the sustainability of those returns as we look out to 2028 and beyond. So, for us, it's really a balance. As we look at these investments, we do feel like it's the right time for us to do it, in part because of the momentum that we see that allows us to undertake them without disturbing our commitments to the outside world. But also that we have businesses that are primed for change, and they are able to absorb that degree of activity, as Venkat called out before, using USCB as an example. And clearly, we have a degree of execution discipline now that we've demonstrated over the last few years. So, we think it is the right time to do it, and as we go through the plan, you will see a balance of investment in the top line, investment to drive efficiency in this way, while still delivering progressive returns and progressive distributions. In terms of USCB, look, we're trying to focus more on total income in this business, because the addition of Best Egg does make it a bit more of a complex mix. I think we get to 20% eventually, but clearly that's going to take some time for us to build, because what we are doing is we are originating balances through Best Egg, and we're building up that that managed portfolio, if you like. But in terms of the overall income trajectory of that business, we have considerable confidence in it for all of the reasons that Venkat outlined. Okay, thank you, Amit. Perhaps we could go to the next question, please.",
  "reason": "The answer directly addresses the bank's investment strategy and the expectations for USCB income, providing a clear explanation and aligning with the question's topics."
}
